items.title: An m-covered family gives every member a certificate of size m plus one
items.author: Gilad Chase; Neta Dafni; Yuval Filmus; Nathan Lindzey
items.work: Uniqueness for 2-Intersecting Families of Permutations and Perfect Matchings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 581-585: if the family is covered by m cosets and the characteristic function has degree at most one after the restriction forced by that covering, then every member has a certificate of the form given by the m prescribed images together with one more image, so the common certificate size is at most m plus one. The proof (source lines 586-602) is a reduction argument that the statement does not display: fixing the coset restricts the function to the remaining coordinates, the degree-one classification applies to that restriction, and the resulting small certificate has to be lifted back through the covering to produce the certificate named in the statement. The statement records only the size bound.
